params.input_content: A command-line calculator application that evaluates arithmetic expressions with basic operations (+, -, *, /), operator precedence, and parentheses. It parses string expressions, computes results rounded to two decimal places, and handles errors gracefully (division by zero, invalid expressions). The code includes full type annotations and docstrings.

project_summary.name: Python Command-Line Calculator
project_summary.description: A command-line calculator application that evaluates arithmetic expressions with basic operations (+, -, *, /), operator precedence, and parentheses. It parses string expressions, computes results rounded to two decimal places, and handles errors gracefully (division by zero, invalid expressions). The code includes full type annotations and docstrings.
project_summary.target_users: End users who need a simple command-line calculator for basic arithmetic.
business_goals: Provide a reliable and accurate calculator tool
Maintain code quality with type annotations and documentation

entities.name: Expression
entities.description: A string representing an arithmetic expression to be evaluated.

attributes.name: raw
attributes.constraints: non-empty, valid characters: digits, operators, parentheses, spaces

attributes.name: result
attributes.description: Computed result rounded to 2 decimal places

entities.name: Calculator
entities.description: Core engine that parses and evaluates expressions.

actors.name: User
actors.description: Person interacting with the calculator via command line.
goals: Enter an arithmetic expression and get the result

functional_requirements.name: Expression Input
functional_requirements.description: The application shall accept a string expression from the command line.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: User can type an expression and press Enter.
AC2: Input is read as a string.

functional_requirements.name: Basic Arithmetic Operations
functional_requirements.description: The application shall support addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), and division (/).

functional_requirements.name: Operator Precedence
functional_requirements.description: The application shall respect standard operator precedence: multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.

functional_requirements.name: Parentheses
functional_requirements.description: The application shall support parentheses to override precedence.

functional_requirements.name: Result Formatting
functional_requirements.description: The application shall return the result rounded to two decimal places.

functional_requirements.name: Error Handling - Division by Zero
functional_requirements.description: The application shall display an error message when division by zero is attempted.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Expression '1/0' shows error message 'Error: Division by zero'
AC2: Expression '0/0' shows error message 'Error: Division by zero'

functional_requirements.name: Error Handling - Invalid Expression
functional_requirements.description: The application shall display an error message for invalid or malformed expressions.

functional_requirements.name: Exit Command
functional_requirements.description: The application shall support an exit command to terminate the program.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Typing 'exit' or 'quit' terminates the program

non_functional_requirements.name: Accuracy
non_functional_requirements.description: All calculations must be accurate to two decimal places.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Results are rounded to 2 decimal places
AC2: Floating point precision issues are handled

non_functional_requirements.name: Performance
non_functional_requirements.description: Expression evaluation should complete in under 100ms for typical expressions.
acceptance_criteria: AC2: Complex expressions with nested parentheses evaluate in < 100ms

non_functional_requirements.name: Code Quality
non_functional_requirements.description: Source code must include complete type annotations and Google-style docstrings.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: All function signatures have type hints
AC2: All public functions have docstrings

non_functional_requirements.name: Usability
non_functional_requirements.description: The command-line interface should be intuitive and provide helpful error messages.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Error messages are descriptive and user-friendly
AC2: The prompt clearly indicates the application is ready for input

use_cases.name: Evaluate Simple Expression
use_cases.description: User enters a simple arithmetic expression and receives the result.
main_flow: Application displays the result rounded to 2 decimal places
error_flows: If expression is invalid, display error message
If division by zero, display error message

use_cases.name: Evaluate Expression with Precedence
use_cases.description: User enters an expression with mixed operators and precedence is respected.
main_flow: Application evaluates with correct precedence (multiplication before addition)

use_cases.name: Evaluate Expression with Parentheses
use_cases.description: User enters an expression with parentheses to override precedence.

risk_assessment.description: Floating point precision errors in arithmetic operations
risk_assessment.mitigation: Round results to 2 decimal places; use Decimal for critical calculations

risk_assessment.description: Incorrect parsing of complex expressions with nested parentheses
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement robust tokenizer and parser with comprehensive test coverage

risk_assessment.description: Performance degradation with very long expressions
risk_assessment.mitigation: Set reasonable input length limits; optimize parsing algorithm

risk_assessment.description: Code injection via eval() or exec() if used for expression evaluation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement custom parser instead of using eval(); validate all input tokens against whitelist of allowed characters

risk_assessment.description: Denial of service via deeply nested parentheses causing stack overflow
risk_assessment.mitigation: Set maximum recursion depth limit; implement iterative parsing as alternative

risk_assessment.description: Input buffer overflow or memory exhaustion from extremely long input strings
risk_assessment.mitigation: Enforce maximum input length (e.g., 1000 characters); validate input before processing

risk_assessment.description: Unicode or special character injection causing parser errors or unexpected behavior
risk_assessment.mitigation: Strict input validation; only allow digits, operators, parentheses, spaces, and decimal points

  12|5. **结果展示**：计算结果保留 2 位小数
  13|

  15|- 使用 Python 3.10+ 编写
  16|- 包含完整的 docstring 文档注释
  17|- 包含完整的类型标注（type hints）
  18|- 优雅处理边界情况
  19|
  20|## 验收标准
  21|- 3 + 4 = 7.00
  22|- 10 - 5 = 5.00
  23|- 6 * 7 = 42.00
  24|- 15 / 3 = 5.00
  25|- 10 / 0 返回清晰错误信息
  26|- "abc + 5" 这类非法输入返回清晰错误信息
  27|- 3 + 4 * 2 = 11.00（优先级正确）
  28|- (3 + 4) * 2 = 14.00（括号支持）
  29|

project_summary.name: Python Command-Line Calculator
project_summary.description: A command-line calculator application that evaluates arithmetic expressions with basic operations (+, -, *, /), operator precedence, and parentheses. It parses string expressions, computes results rounded to two decimal places, and handles errors gracefully (division by zero, invalid expressions). The code includes full type annotations and docstrings.
project_summary.target_users: End users who need a simple command-line calculator for basic arithmetic.
business_goals: Provide a reliable and accurate calculator tool
Maintain code quality with type annotations and documentation

entities.name: Expression
entities.description: A string representing an arithmetic expression to be evaluated.

attributes.name: raw
attributes.constraints: non-empty, valid characters: digits, operators, parentheses, spaces

attributes.name: result
attributes.description: Computed result rounded to 2 decimal places

entities.name: Calculator
entities.description: Core engine that parses and evaluates expressions.

actors.name: User
actors.description: Person interacting with the calculator via command line.
goals: Enter an arithmetic expression and get the result

functional_requirements.name: Expression Input
functional_requirements.description: The application shall accept a string expression from the command line.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: User can type an expression and press Enter.
AC2: Input is read as a string.

functional_requirements.name: Basic Arithmetic Operations
functional_requirements.description: The application shall support addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), and division (/).

functional_requirements.name: Operator Precedence
functional_requirements.description: The application shall respect standard operator precedence: multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.

functional_requirements.name: Parentheses
functional_requirements.description: The application shall support parentheses to override precedence.

functional_requirements.name: Result Formatting
functional_requirements.description: The application shall return the result rounded to two decimal places.

functional_requirements.name: Error Handling - Division by Zero

project_summary.name: Command-Line Arithmetic Calculator
project_summary.description: A command-line calculator application that evaluates arithmetic expressions with basic operations (+, -, *, /), operator precedence, and parentheses. It parses string expressions, computes results rounded to two decimal places, and handles errors gracefully (division by zero, invalid expressions). The code includes full type annotations and docstrings.
project_summary.target_users: Developers and users who need a simple, accurate command-line calculator for arithmetic expressions.
business_goals: Provide a reliable tool for evaluating arithmetic expressions
Ensure correct operator precedence and parentheses handling
Deliver clear error messages for invalid input
Maintain high code quality with type annotations and docstrings

entities.name: Expression
entities.description: A string representing an arithmetic expression to be evaluated.

attributes.name: tokens
attributes.constraints: each token is a number or operator or parenthesis

attributes.name: ast
attributes.description: Abstract syntax tree representing the expression

attributes.name: result
attributes.description: Computed result rounded to two decimal places

entities.name: Token
entities.description: A lexical unit of the expression.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: Type of token: NUMBER, OPERATOR, LPAREN, RPAREN

entities.name: Node
entities.description: A node in the abstract syntax tree.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Value if NUMBER, operator symbol if OPERATOR

actors.name: User
actors.description: A person who uses the command-line calculator to evaluate arithmetic expressions.
goals: Enter an arithmetic expression and receive the computed result

functional_requirements.name: Tokenization
functional_requirements.description: The system shall tokenize the input expression string into a list of tokens (numbers, operators, parentheses).
acceptance_criteria: AC4: Invalid characters (e.g., letters) raise an error

functional_requirements.name: Parsing and AST Construction
functional_requirements.description: The system shall parse the token list into an abstract syntax tree (AST) respecting operator precedence and parentheses.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Expression '2+3*4' yields AST with * as root of right subtree
AC2: Expression '(2+3)*4' yields AST with + as left child of *
AC3: Expression '5' yields a single number node

functional_requirements.name: Evaluation
functional_requirements.description: The system shall evaluate the AST and compute the numeric result, rounding to two decimal places.

functional_requirements.name: Error Handling
functional_requirements.description: The system shall detect and report errors: division by zero, invalid expressions, mismatched parentheses, invalid characters.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: '1/0' raises ZeroDivisionError with message 'Division by zero'
AC2: '1+*2' raises ValueError with message 'Invalid expression'
AC3: '(1+2' raises ValueError with message 'Mismatched parentheses'
AC4: 'a+2' raises ValueError with message 'Invalid character'

functional_requirements.name: Command-Line Interface
functional_requirements.description: The system shall accept an expression as a command-line argument and print the result or error message.
acceptance_criteria: AC2: Running 'calc "1/0"' prints 'Error: Division by zero'
AC3: Running 'calc' with no argument prints usage information

nonfunctional_requirements.name: Response Time
nonfunctional_requirements.description: The calculator shall evaluate any valid expression within 100 milliseconds.
nonfunctional_requirements.target_metric: Average response time < 100ms for expressions up to 100 characters

nonfunctional_requirements.name: Error Messages
nonfunctional_requirements.description: Error messages shall be clear and descriptive, indicating the nature of the error.
nonfunctional_requirements.target_metric: User can understand the error without external documentation

nonfunctional_requirements.name: Code Documentation
nonfunctional_requirements.description: All functions and classes shall have docstrings and type annotations.
nonfunctional_requirements.target_metric: 100% of public functions have docstrings and type annotations

nonfunctional_requirements.name: Correctness
nonfunctional_requirements.description: The calculator shall produce mathematically correct results for all valid expressions.
nonfunctional_requirements.target_metric: Pass a suite of 100 test cases covering precedence, parentheses, and edge cases

use_cases.name: Evaluate Arithmetic Expression
preconditions: The calculator application is installed and accessible from command line.
main_flow: 5. System evaluates AST to compute result.
6. System rounds result to two decimal places.
7. System prints the result to stdout.

alternative_flows.condition: If tokenization fails due to invalid characters
flow: 3b. System prints error message: 'Error: Invalid character'.

alternative_flows.condition: If parsing fails due to mismatched parentheses or invalid expression
flow: 4b. System prints error message: 'Error: Invalid expression' or 'Error: Mismatched parentheses'.

alternative_flows.condition: If evaluation encounters division by zero
flow: 5b. System prints error message: 'Error: Division by zero'.

alternative_flows.condition: If no expression argument is provided

postconditions: The result or error message is displayed to the user.
business_rules: Operator precedence: * and / have higher precedence than + and -.
Result is rounded to two decimal places using standard rounding (half up).

constraints.description: The application must be implemented in Python 3.8+.
The application must run on Windows, macOS, and Linux command lines.
No external dependencies beyond Python standard library.

risk_assessment.risk: Incorrect handling of operator precedence leading to wrong results
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement a well-tested shunting-yard algorithm or recursive descent parser.
risk_assessment.contingency: Add comprehensive unit tests for precedence scenarios.

risk_assessment.mitigation: Use Decimal for intermediate calculations or round only at the end.
risk_assessment.contingency: Accept rounding to two decimals as specification.

risk_assessment.risk: Performance issues with very long expressions
risk_assessment.contingency: Set a reasonable input length limit (e.g., 1000 characters).

assumptions: Input expressions are provided as a single command-line argument enclosed in quotes.
Numbers can be integers or decimals (e.g., 5.5).
Spaces in the expression are ignored.
The application will be used interactively or in scripts.

   1|# 简易计算器应用需求文档
   2|
   3|## 概述
   4|构建一个基于 Python 的计算器应用，支持基本算术运算。
   5|
   6|## 功能需求
   7|
   8|1. **基本运算**：支持加法 (+)、减法 (-)、乘法 (*)、除法 (/)
   9|2. **输入处理**：接受字符串格式的数学表达式（例如 "3 + 4 * 2"）
  10|3. **运算符优先级**：遵循标准数学优先级（乘除优先于加减），支持括号
  11|4. **错误处理**：对除零和无效输入返回清晰的错误信息
  12|5. **结果展示**：计算结果保留 2 位小数
  13|
  14|## 非功能需求
  15|- 使用 Python 3.10+ 编写
  16|- 包含完整的 docstring 文档注释
  17|- 包含完整的类型标注（type hints）
  18|- 优雅处理边界情况
  19|
  20|## 验收标准
  21|- 3 + 4 = 7.00
  22|- 10 - 5 = 5.00
  23|- 6 * 7 = 42.00
  24|- 15 / 3 = 5.00
  25|- 10 / 0 返回清晰错误信息
  26|- "abc + 5" 这类非法输入返回清晰错误信息
  27|- 3 + 4 * 2 = 11.00（优先级正确）
  28|- (3 + 4) * 2 = 14.00（括号支持）
  29|
